children: What Happened?
A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after investors shifted their focus from what AI technology can do toward concerns over how companies will finance it.

Driven by these escalating AI funding fears and elevated interest rates, CNBC noted that a massive rotation out of the sector erased more than $1 trillion from the world's largest semiconductor and AI-related stocks this week. Furthermore, CNBC explained that this funding anxiety triggered counterintuitive moves in the broader market, as investors reassessed the impact of high interest rates on corporate debt-servicing capacity and overall economic growth. Because of these rising structural risks, CNBC reported that safe-haven demand temporarily outweighed inflation fears, prompting capital to exit high-growth tech assets and flow into the Treasury market, which ironically pulled the 10-year Treasury yield down toward 5.09 percent.

Ultimately, according to CNBC analysts, this widespread tech sell-off underscores a growing realization on Wall Street that if the capital-intensive AI trade slows due to financing constraints, broader economic growth will likely decelerate as well.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

Zooming In On Samsara (IOT)

Samsara’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 42 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 11 days ago when the stock gained 3.5% on the news that softer labor market data tempered expectations for an October interest rate increase by the Federal Reserve. The latest employment figures signaled a gradual cooling in workforce demand, prompting investors to scale back forecasts of tighter monetary policy from the central bank. When labor market pressures ease, policymakers face less wage-driven inflation risk, reducing the likelihood of additional borrowing cost increases. For growth-oriented technology businesses, lower projected interest rates are particularly beneficial because their market valuations rely heavily on projected future cash flows. When discount rates stabilize or decline, the present value of those future earnings increases, supporting valuations across the sector as market participants await the release of the Federal Reserve's policy minutes.

Samsara is up 16% since the beginning of the year, but at $39.36 per share, it is still trading 13% below its 52-week high of $45.22 from December 2025. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Samsara’s shares at the IPO in December 2021 would now be looking at an investment worth $1,594.
